title: Six Main Roads to Change: Broad Boulevards as Smart Shortcuts
coreMove: Choose the one influence principle that honestly fits the choice and make it salient before the request.
sourcePressure: The source identifies reciprocity, liking, authority, social proof, scarcity, and consistency as broad influence shortcuts that can be frontloaded.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Cycle through six persuasion tricks until one gets compliance.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator choosing reciprocity before a membership ask
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a small useful loan should come before the fee request
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator hands residents a free blade-sharpening voucher before showing the annual membership card
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sharpening voucher beside a row of loaner drills

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer choosing authority before a clinical guideline session
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether credentials must be salient before the recommendation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer places the speaker’s trial role on the badge slide before the protocol ask appears
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a badge slide with one credential line highlighted

exampleSpecs.audience: a CSA manager choosing scarcity before late-season renewals
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether limited beds are real and should be named before signup
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager shows the actual field map with only twelve winter beds left before opening renewals
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated field map with twelve beds circled

exampleSpecs.audience: a director choosing consistency before asking for rehearsals
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether members should recall their own standard before committing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director asks singers to mark the performance they promised not to miss before handing out the rehearsal calendar
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rehearsal calendar under a pencil-written performance date

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer choosing social proof before home assessments
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visible neighbor participation lowers uncertainty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer places a map of signed-up roofs beside the assessment form before mentioning rebates
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a neighborhood map dotted with roof stickers

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator choosing liking before compliance with booth rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether shared taste should be visible before a hard constraint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the curator comments on one maker’s material choice from the application before explaining the strict booth footprint
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sample swatch beside a booth-layout card

skillTargets: frontload only the principle that honestly fits

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one request and choose a single principle from reciprocity, liking, authority, social proof, scarcity, or consistency that honestly fits before you frame it.
